parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no documented universal-exposure measure (no facility, custody, border or care restriction), no state targeting, and legal gender recognition plus comprehensive antidiscrimination law signal a trans-respecting institutional culture. Visitor-facing positives: same-sex conduct lawful, no official-condoned violence reported, organisations can register. Offsetting negatives: enforcement of protections is 'very rarely' exercised, the hate-crime framework has documented institutional shortcomings, victims rely on civil society, and documented societal hostility at Pride (assaults, eggs, flag burnings) with a slow interior-ministerial response shows weak remedy — tier 3, not tier 1/2. Bias counts are raw, undenominated counts; violence is under-recorded, which is neither strong evidence of safety nor of a campaign. Absent documented border or facility friction, this sits in Reduced Risk with residual friction and thin recourse.
